papers.title: Slow-Wave Enhancement Reduces Axonal Injury in Murine Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major cause of death and disability as well as impaired cognition and sleep-wake abnormalities. The pathological hallmark of TBI is disturbed axonal transport and accumulation of proteins, leading to diffuse axonal injury (DAI). Recent studies suggest a role for slow-wave sleep (SWS) in the clearance of harmful extracellular proteins and functional recovery. Our group previously found that increasing SWS after TBI in rats improved cognition and decreased accumulation of injury-related histological markers in cortex and hippocampus, indicating a neuroprotective role of SWS. Though growing evidence suggests that sleep can improve the outcome of TBI, prior mouse models of TBI were incompatible with sleep recordings. In the current study, we modified the classical weight-drop mouse model to be compatible with a headset for recording electroencephalogram (EEG) and electromyogram, and to replicate effects of SWS modulation on TBI outcome measures. The resulting mild TBI mouse model shows cognitive impairment, EEG abnormalities, and DAI. Such DAI was reduced following treatment with sodium oxybate during the first 3 days after trauma, concomitant with increased slow-wave activity. Chemogenetic modulation of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons, on the other hand, did not reduce slow-wave activity. Overall, in the present study, we characterized an adapted weight-drop mouse TBI model for studying the relationship between sleep and TBI and provided additional evidence on involvement of sleep in neuronal recovery.

papers.title: State-dependent gating of sensory and cortical inputs by median raphe neurons
papers.abstract: The mesopontine median raphe (MnR) plays an important role in regulating brain states, hippocampal network activity, and memory processes. Recent studies have revealed that the MnR comprises three major neuronal populations: serotonergic (5-HT), glutamatergic (Vglut3-expressing), and GABAergic neurons. How these distinct neuronal populations may gate sensory and cortical inputs across different brain states remains largely unknown. Here, we combined in vivo electrophysiological recording, sensory or optogenetic stimulation, and transgenic approaches to characterize the response properties of 5-HT, Vglut3, and GABAergic MnR neurons during wakefulness and sleep. We found that MnR neurons exhibited pronounced state-dependent responses to both sensory and cortical stimulation, with response amplitudes significantly greater during slow-wave sleep than during wakefulness. Auditory and somatosensory stimuli elicited fast responses in the MnR: 5-HT neurons were primarily suppressed, whereas Vglut3 and GABAergic neurons were primarily activated, suggesting the presence of direct inputs from sensory thalamic or brainstem structures. Retrograde tracing identified several brainstem structures and, notably, the medial prefrontal cortex as sources of direct projections to the MnR. Optogenetic stimulation of prefrontal inputs to the MnR evoked inhibition of 5-HT neurons but robust excitation of Vglut3 neurons during slow-wave sleep, suggesting top-down control of MnR activity by the prefrontal cortex. Together, these findings reveal that the MnR exhibits enhanced sensitivity to both ascending sensory and descending cortical inputs during sleep, suggesting that it may integrate environmental and cortical signals to regulate hippocampal network activity and gate sleep-dependent memory processing.

papers.title: Ideal sleep duration as a potential explanation of the bimodal chronotype: An exploratory study.
papers.abstract: Regarding circadian typology, the existence of a fourth category, the bimodal types, was previously proposed. Bimodal types would be those answering some questions as morning types, while others as evening types, resulting in a different sleep-wake cycle compared to intermediate types. The aim of this study was to further explore the plausibility of this new circadian typology category, attempting to determine whether it qualifies as a genuinely new category of individuals or merely a byproduct of another individual difference, namely ideal sleep duration. To this end, we reanalyzed data previously collected from 1583 children and adolescents (817 females, mean age of 13.13 ± 1.96) and 2115 adults (1144 females, mean age of 44.50 ± 5.64) who completed the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire for Children and Adolescents (MEQ-CA) and the MEQ, respectively. The open-ended questions on the ideal bedtime and get-up time were used to compute the ideal total sleep time that was later grouped into three categories: short- (≤6 hours), medium- (6 < x < 12 hours), and long sleepers (≥12 hours). In children and adolescents, bimodal types were overrepresented in both short and long sleepers and underrepresented among medium sleepers; separately considering the gender variable, the same pattern of results was detected in males only. Regarding adults, an overrepresentation of bimodal types was observed among long sleepers and their underrepresentation among medium sleepers; this same distribution was replicated only in males. It seems that the suggested fourth category of circadian typology, that of bimodal types, may be considered as a byproduct of the individual difference in ideal sleep duration.

papers.title: Pooled sequencing reveals patterns of underlying genomic divergence in Drosophila chronotypes
papers.abstract: Chronotypes, often referred to in the context of sleep timing in humans (early/late sleepers) are heritable variations in timing of circadian behaviours. Chronotype differences among individuals have been associated with a myriad of psychological, metabolic, and physiological dysregulations. Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS) in humans have identified several circadian clock gene polymorphisms associated with divergent chronotypes; however, the lists of candidate genes vary across studies based on methodology and sampling strategy thus, necessitating more controlled studies on well-established model systems. Using long-term experimental evolution approach spanning over 20 years, we have derived a unique set of chronotypes in the form of 12 replicate Drosophila melanogaster populations that exhibit early/morning and late/evening emergence and have previously reported several circadian clock differences between the populations. We performed pooled DNA sequencing to explore genomic differences underlying early and late chronotypes and identified multiple genomic regions under selection. We observe that the early chronotype populations have primarily accumulated polymorphisms in genes related to photosensitivity, sleep, and the circadian clock, while the late chronotype populations have largely accumulated polymorphisms in genes related to the circadian clock, mRNA splicing mechanisms, and ecdysis. We further predict biological pathways under differential selection in the early and late chronotype populations. We believe these results provide evolutionary mechanisms behind chronotype divergence and will help generate verifiable hypothesis regarding target genes for phase divergence.

papers.title: EEG-Derived Proxies of Cortical Excitability in Epilepsy: Group Discrimination, Temporal Stability and Medication Sensitivity
papers.abstract: Objective To identify EEG-derived markers of cortical excitability that best distinguish people with epilepsy from healthy controls while maintaining stability across repeated recordings, and to assess the influence of antiseizure medication (ASM) burden on these measures. Methods Scalp EEG recordings from the Temple University Hospital EEG Epilepsy Corpus were analyzed, including 1,404 recordings from 96 individuals with neurologist-confirmed epilepsy and 85 healthy controls across multiple sessions. Eight global EEG measures were evaluated: aperiodic exponent and offset, sample entropy, detrended fluctuation analysis exponent and derived index, spatial gamma-band phase consistency, and absolute and relative alpha power. Primary group inference used linear mixed-effects models to account for repeated recordings and sessions within participants. Secondary analyses examined group differences in measures temporal stability and cross-metric correlation. We examined only in epilepsy group associations between EEG-derived metrics and ASMs count, and their impact on cross-metric correlations. Results In the mixed-effects models, aperiodic offset and exponent were the only measures with FDR-robust group effects. Aperiodic offset showed higher consistency in epilepsy than in healthy controls (standardized epilepsy-minus-healthy beta = 0.52, 95% CI 0.25 to 0.78, FDR-adjusted p = 0.001). Across sessions, consistency was higher in epilepsy for aperiodic offset exponent (beta = 0.32, 95% CI 0.10 to 0.54, FDR-adjusted p = 0.018). Cross-metric correlation patterns were largely preserved between groups. Medication associations were examined separately within the epilepsy group. Higher ASM burden was associated with higher alpha relative power. Significance Among eight candidate EEG measures aperiodic offset and exponent differed between groups (epilepsy vs. healthy controls), and both were more reproducible across sessions in epilepsy. Relative alpha power tracked within-person antiseizure medication burden, suggesting that disease-related and treatment-related EEG markers may be complementary. These findings, obtained from routine clinical EEG in an open dataset, suggest aperiodic spectral parameters as candidates for prospective validation as biomarkers.

papers.title: [Research progress on genome-wide association study of circadian chronotype in adolescents].
papers.abstract: Circadian chronotype refers to stable individual differences in sleep-wake cycles and activity timing preferences, and is closely associated with sleep patterns, behavioral characteristics, and mental health. In recent years, with the rapid development of genome-wide association studies (GWAS), increasing attention has been paid to the genetic basis of chronotype. Previous studies have demonstrated that chronotype is highly heritable, and GWAS have identified multiple genetic variants associated with chronotype in adult populations, involving core circadian clock genes, neurotransmitter signaling pathways, and protein degradation regulatory pathways. However, adolescence represents a critical period of circadian development and sleep pattern transition, and the genetic regulation and health implications of chronotype in adolescents remain insufficiently understood. Evening chronotype and delayed circadian timing have been closely associated with insufficient sleep, depression, anxiety, attention deficits, and other mental health problems among adolescents. This review summarizes recent advances in GWAS of chronotype, focusing on its genetic architecture, potential regulatory mechanisms, and current evidence in adolescent populations. Furthermore, the associations between chronotype, sleep characteristics, and mental health outcomes are discussed, providing theoretical insights into the genetic mechanisms underlying adolescent circadian changes and their health implications, and supporting the development of individualized prevention and intervention strategies.

papers.title: Wearable-based sleep and activity tracking detects Parkinson's disease and associated pathological hallmarks
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is associated with sleep and motor function impairment, even in the early stages. Here, we investigated whether passive wearable-based sleep and activity tracking can detect PD and its associated pathological hallmarks, dopaminergic deficit and -synuclein pathology. Sleep and activity metrics (SAM) were derived from free-living wrist accelerometry data of a U.S. cohort and used to train a machine learning model (SAM-PD) to distinguish persons with PD (n = 133) from healthy controls (n = 26). The model achieved an AUROC of 0.93 and an AUPRC of 0.98, demonstrated excellent test-retest reliability, and generalized without retraining to an independent European cohort (n = 40; 50% PwPD) monitored with a different device (AUROC, 0.95; AUPRC, 0.95). REM sleep duration, walking cadence, and low-level acceleration features were most predictive. Applied to a U.S. at-risk cohort, SAM-PD performed comparably to the resource-intensive Movement Disorder Society (MDS) prodromal PD risk score in detecting dopaminergic deficit (AUROC, 0.86 vs. 0.80; AUPRC, 0.45 vs. 0.46; n = 121; 12.4% prevalence) and -synuclein pathology (AUROC, 0.76 for both; AUPRC 0.50 vs. 0.42; n = 114; 16.7% prevalence). A combination with the MDS score modestly improved detection. Findings support further evaluation of wearable monitoring for PD screening and biomarker enrichment in larger populations.

papers.title: The Effect of Nursing-Implemented Swaddling and Dim Light on Sleep Patterns and Weight Gain in Preterm Infants: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
papers.abstract: BackgroundPreterm infants admitted to neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) are highly vulnerable to sleep disruption caused by environmental stressors such as excessive light exposure, frequent handling, and routine caregiving procedures. Disturbed sleep may negatively affect neurodevelopment, physiological stability, and growth. Developmentally supportive nursing interventions, including swaddling and environmental light reduction, are intended to minimise sensory stress and support behavioural regulation. ObjectivesTo evaluate the association of nursing-implemented swaddling combined with dim light exposure with sleep patterns and short-term weight gain among preterm infants. DesignQuasi-experimental controlled study with repeated measurements. MethodsThe study was conducted on a purposive sample of 60 preterm infants allocated to an intervention group (n = 30) and a control group (n = 30). Infants in the intervention group received standardised swaddling and dim light exposure during designated rest periods in addition to routine NICU care, whereas the control group received routine care only. Sleep-wake behavioural organisation was assessed daily for five consecutive days using the Anderson Behavioral State Scoring System (ABSS), and body weight was measured daily using a calibrated electronic infant scale. Data were analysed using non-parametric statistical tests, including the Mann-Whitney U, Wilcoxon signed-rank, and Friedman tests. ResultsBaseline characteristics were comparable between groups for gestational age, birth weight, baseline weight, and APGAR scores; however, postnatal age was significantly higher in the intervention group (p = .004). Infants receiving swaddling and dim light demonstrated significantly greater improvements in sleep-wake behavioural organisation across the five-day study period than infants receiving routine care (all p < .001). The intervention group also showed significantly higher mean body weight at Day 5 (p = .009) and a higher mean discharge weight. ConclusionNursing-implemented swaddling combined with dim light exposure was associated with improved sleep-wake behavioural organisation and higher mean body weight at Day 5 and discharge among preterm infants, supporting the incorporation of developmentally supportive nursing practices into routine NICU care.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm in the atrioventricular node - in electrophysiology, contractility, metabolism, intracellular signalling and extracellular matrix
papers.abstract: The atrioventricular (AV) node shows a circadian rhythm-during sleep the PR interval is longer (because conduction velocity is decreased) and AV block is more common. We show the rhythm is similar in mouse and human, and using mice we have investigated the cause. There was still a rhythm in Kcnj5 knockout mice ruling out a major role of vagal tone (the vagus regulates the node via Kcnj5). Instead, we show the presence of a functioning circadian clock in the node (e.g. by detection of rhythmic clock transcripts). There was ~43-52% reduction in the rhythm of the PR interval on inhibition of the clock in a Bmal1 knockout mouse. There was a significant rhythm in >300 intracellular signalling molecules presumably driven by the clock and perhaps extrinsic signals. Downstream of the clock and signalling molecules, there was a rhythm in many transcripts and proteins (of 4,186 proteins, ~15% had a rhythm), responsible for example for contractile machinery, metabolism, extracellular matrix, and importantly ion channels. Ultimately, the PR interval is determined by ion channels, and there were rhythms in ion channels and ionic currents. A key determinant of conduction velocity is the upstroke velocity of the Ca2+-dependent nodal action potential and this was significantly reduced during sleep, this can be explained by reduced expression of Ca2+ channel subunits and a smaller L-type Ca2+ current at this time and this was confirmed by biophysically-detailed computer modelling. In conclusion, there is day-night molecular remodelling of the AV node and this is largely responsible for the circadian rhythm in the PR interval.

papers.title: Associations of Serum Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid and Docosahexaenoic Acid Levels with Pediatric Sleep Disorders: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
papers.abstract: This study investigates the serum levels of γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) among children with sleep disorders, to generate preliminary hypotheses for future research. A total of 95 consecutively enrolled children newly diagnosed with sleep disorders from January to July 2024 were included in this cross-sectional observational study. Blood GABA and DHA levels were measured using API 4500 liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry system. Sleep disorders were classified by physicians according to ICSD-3 criteria based on structured parental interviews supplemented by brief sleep habit questions, without objective sleep monitoring such as polysomnography or actigraphy. No significant differences in GABA and DHA serum levels were found between genders. Within these children diagnosed with sleep disorders, significant inter-age differences in serum GABA and DHA were observed, younger patients exhibited higher serum GABA and DHA relative to older patients in the same clinical sample. Children with insomnia showed lower serum GABA than those with parasomnia (unadjusted for age confounding). A positive correlation between GABA levels and maternal education was observed. No significant difference in DHA was observed between insomnia and parasomnia. Maternal education was positively correlated with GABA in univariate analysis, but this association did not remain significant in multivariable models. Younger children with sleep disorders had higher GABA and DHA serum levels, and children with insomnia had lower GABA than those with parasomnia, whereas no significant difference in DHA was observed between these two groups. These cross-sectional correlational findings cannot establish causality. Definitive evaluation of serum GABA and DHA as candidate biomarkers requires further studies.

papers.title: Development and EEG Assessment of a Virtual Reality Replica of a Prior Real Multisensory Environment Intervention.
papers.abstract: Multisensory environments (MSEs) are valuable therapeutic spaces for relaxation and stress relief, yet high costs and physical infrastructure limit accessibility. Immersive virtual reality MSEs (V-MSEs) offer a low-cost and scalable alternative to real MSEs (R-MSEs), but evidence is scarce. The aim of this study is an exploratory characterization of the electroencephalography (EEG) response to a V-MSE replica of a previous R-MSE intervention, using the original R-MSE data as a qualitative reference. After developing a V-MSE mirroring the original environment, 31 healthy participants underwent an adapted version of the protocol, and spectral and nonlinear features were computed from EEG recordings pre- and post-intervention. Analyses were performed within each environment, and comparisons between them remained qualitative. The alpha/beta ratio, negatively correlated with stress, was the only feature significantly increased in both conditions. In the V-MSE, frontal theta and the theta/beta ratio also increased significantly, whereas relative gamma power and Lempel-Ziv complexity decreased. Only in R-MSE, parieto-occipital alpha power rose significantly, whereas frontal delta power decreased. No feature changed significantly in opposite directions between settings. Evidence remains insufficient to establish V-MSEs as an alternative to R-MSEs, but this first EEG characterization of a V-MSE is encouraging enough to justify broader studies.

papers.title: Spectral power and functional connectivity alterations in multiple system atrophy revealed by resting-state EEG.
papers.abstract: Multiple system atrophy (MSA) is an aggressive α-synucleinopathy characterized by motor and autonomic dysfunction. Elucidating neurophysiological patterns can provide crucial insights into the underlying neural mechanisms. Resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) and fMRI data were collected from 69 healthy controls and 123 MSA patients, comprising a discovery cohort (n = 97) and an independent validation cohort (n = 26). MSA patients showed reduced delta power in the cerebellar, frontoparietal, visual I, and limbic networks, with widespread increases in theta and high gamma power. Amplitude-based connectivity decreased across the alpha, beta, and gamma bands in subcortical, cerebellar, default mode, motor, and visual I networks, with increased theta-band synchrony involving motor, visual II, and frontoparietal networks. These EEG abnormalities were corroborated by fMRI connectivity, highlighting cross-modal consistency. Canonical correlation analysis revealed associations between EEG features and motor/non-motor symptom severity. Interpretable stacking models accurately classified MSA-C and MSA-P subtypes and predicted UMSARS progression in longitudinal follow-up. These findings identified aberrant neural activity and network dysfunction in MSA, highlighting EEG as a promising biomarker for disease monitoring.

papers.title: Transcriptomic and behavioral analyses link perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA) exposure to circadian and visual pathway disruption in larval zebrafish (Danio rerio).
papers.abstract: Perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA) is a short-chain perfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) detected in fish tissues and environmental matrices, yet its mechanisms of toxicity remain poorly understood. We evaluated developmental, behavioral, and transcriptomic responses in zebrafish (Danio rerio) exposed to 0.1-100µg/L PFBA for seven days. Survival remained above 96%, although a slight reduction (~2%) was observed in exposed groups. Hatching rate and reactive oxygen species levels were unaffected. Behavioral analysis revealed hypoactivity at 0.1 and 1µg/L, restricted to the first dark and first light periods, indicating a non-monotonic concentration-response. RNA-seq identified 3,177, 1,919, and 2,277 differentially expressed transcripts at 0.1, 1, and 10µg/L, respectively. Exposure to 1µg/L altered circadian rhythm and photoperiodism pathways, whereas 10µg/L affected the nervous system, visual perception, and lens development. Circadian-related genes (cry2, cry3b, cryba1a) were differentially expressed, supporting transcriptomic findings and providing mechanistic insight into PFBA-induced behavioral alterations.

papers.title: Multiscale neural and endocrine control of CD8⁺ T cell fate in cancer: from systemic physiology to local immune circuits.
papers.abstract: CD8⁺ T cells are central cytotoxic effectors of anti-tumor immunity, but tumor-infiltrating CD8⁺ populations are functionally heterogeneous and include tumor-reactive, dysfunctional, and bystander states. Although the past decade of cancer immunology has focused largely on how local interactions within the tumor microenvironment shape these states, clinical observations linking chronic stress, sleep disruption, endocrine comorbidity, and circadian timing to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) outcomes indicate that CD8⁺ T cell function is also modulated far beyond the tumor itself. In this review we adopt a whole-organism perspective to examine how autonomic and sensory neural circuits and the endocrine system act across anatomical compartments to govern CD8⁺ T cell priming, trafficking, metabolism, and exhaustion. We first analyze sympathetic, parasympathetic, and sensory neural axes as systemic effectors mediated by catecholamines, acetylcholine, neuropeptides, and brainstem-driven tone. We then examine endocrine regulation through the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, metabolic hormones, and gonadal steroids. We integrate these axes within the tumor microenvironment, where nerve-derived signals, paracrine neuropeptides, and locally amplified glucocorticoid activity form a convergent suppressive network, and at the organismal level through stress amplification loops, sex dimorphism, gut-relayed microbial signaling, and circadian timing. Collectively, this evidence identifies neuro-endocrine signaling as an actionable, mechanistically stratified layer of systemic immune regulation and supports its evaluation as a source of biomarkers and pharmacological targets for sensitizing tumors to ICI therapy. This framework offered here is intended to bridge cancer neuroscience, endocrine oncology, and immunotherapy, and to define the criteria by which the next generation of systems-level immune sensitizers should be evaluated.

papers.title: Daridorexant in treatment refractory cluster headache: A retrospective case series.
papers.abstract: Cluster headache (CH) is one of the most excruciating pain conditions known in humans. Most patients experience nocturnal attacks, which further worsen sleep quality and overall quality of life. The management of CH includes acute and preventive treatments, and in some cases, transitional therapy with corticosteroids may be used to achieve pain freedom in a shorter time while giving preventive therapy. We report our preliminary experience with daridorexant, a selective dual orexin receptor antagonist approved for chronic insomnia, as an adjunctive treatment in patients with treatment refractory CH, nocturnal attacks, and bad quality of sleep. Our objective was to describe within-patient changes in nocturnal attack frequency, sleep quality, and headache-related disability before and after add-on daridorexant in refractory CH. In this single-center, retrospective before-after case series, we reviewed clinical data from 10 patients followed at the Headache Center of the San Carlo Borromeo Hospital in Milan (Italy) between June 2023 and December 2024, with a diagnosis of either episodic or chronic CH, who experienced nocturnal attacks, sleep disturbances, and with inadequate response to standard treatments, including verapamil, lithium, or corticosteroids. In these patients, daridorexant was administered as add-on therapy, to treat the chronic insomnia. The frequency and features of CH attacks, sleep quality, headache-related disability, and quality-of-life evaluations were assessed before and after treatment. Treatment with daridorexant was associated with a significant reduction in nocturnal attacks, from 13.1 ± 7.5 to 6.4 ± 7.7 attacks per week (p < 0.050; n = 10/10). Patients also reported improved quality of life, with mean subjective quality-of-life scores increasing from 37% ± 15.6% to 61% ± 20.4% (p = 0.001; n = 10/10). Headache-related impact was reduced, with mean Headache Impact Test 6 scores decreasing from 62.0 ± 7.4 to 48.8 ± 16.2 (p < 0.050; n = 10/10). In addition, no patient reported worsening on the Patient Global Impression of Change scale, and eight of the nine out of 10 available Patient Global Impression of Change ratings indicated improvement. Daridorexant was generally well-tolerated, with adverse events reported in three out of 10 patients (30%), leading to treatment discontinuation in one patient. Daridorexant was significantly associated particularly with a reduction in the number of nocturnal attacks in patients with CH refractory to conventional therapies. These pilot preliminary results suggest a potential role for daridorexant as an adjunctive option for patients with CH, particularly those with a poor response to traditional therapies, nocturnal attacks, and sleep disturbances. Further prospective, controlled studies are warranted to confirm these findings and clarify the mechanisms underlying the observed clinical benefits.

papers.title: Nocturnal hypoxaemic parameters from cardiorespiratory holter monitoring are associated with all-cause mortality in post-ischaemic stroke patients: The CHUTE study.
papers.abstract: Stroke affects approximately 140,000 patients annually in France and is the second leading cause of mortality after cancer. Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), particularly obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), worsens functional recovery and increases mortality risk after stroke. The objective of this study was to evaluate markers of nocturnal hypoxaemia recorded during cardiorespiratory Holter monitoring in patients hospitalised for a first ischaemic stroke and to assess their association with all-cause mortality. We conducted a retrospective, observational, single-centre longitudinal study including adult patients hospitalised for ischaemic stroke at Saint-Etienne University Hospital (January 2010-December 2020) who underwent cardiorespiratory Holter monitoring. papers.abstract: Frontotemporal dementia (FTD) is a neurodegenerative disorder that may initially present with behavioral and affective symptoms, often mimicking primary psychiatric conditions, such as bipolar disorder, leading to frequent misdiagnosis. Neuropsychological evaluation revealed significant executive dysfunction. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated bilateral frontal and anterior temporal lobe atrophy consistent with behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD). This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing late-onset manic syndromes from neurodegenerative disease. It underscores the importance of integrating clinical history, cognitive assessment, and neuroimaging to improve diagnostic accuracy and avoid misdiagnosis.

papers.title: Associations between biomarkers, muscle function, dynapenia status, fall risk, depressive symptoms, and sleep quality in patients with lower limb osteoarthritis: a cross-sectional study.

Multivariable logistic regression analysis revealed that lower Hb levels (odds ratio [OR] = 0.64, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.45-0.91), lower HbA1c levels (OR = 0.57, 95% CI = 0.33-0.99), and higher fall risk scores (OR = 1.14, 95% CI = 1.02-1.28) were independently associated with poor sleep quality. Lower Hb levels, lower HbA1c levels, and higher fall risk were independently associated with poorer sleep quality. papers.title: [Pediatric obstructive sleep apnea syndrome and myofunctional rehabilitation: A preliminary survey of French practitioners].
papers.abstract: Pediatric obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (pOSA) affects 1-5% of children and may lead to significant neurocognitive, metabolic, and cardiovascular morbidity. This preliminary national study aims to assess perceptions and practices related to OMT among different healthcare professionals in France. An 18-item online questionnaire was distributed between March and June 2025 to orthodontists, maxillofacial physiotherapists, and speech therapists. A total of 135 responses were analyzed. The most frequently reported dysfunctions were orofacial hypotonia (91%) and lingual motor immaturity (88%). Interprofessional differences were observed regarding proprioception, cervico-cephalic posture, short upper lip, and relative macroglossia. Physiotherapists emphasized nasal hygiene, whereas orthodontists focused more on orofacial habits and swallowing. Overweight was generally underestimated as an associated factor. The main barriers to OMT implementation included limited access to specialists, lack of training, insufficient interdisciplinary collaboration, and limited recognition of this approach. The observed variations may reflect differences in professional training, terminology, or sampling bias. These results, based on self-reported practices, do not allow assessment of the clinical effectiveness of OMT in pOSA. However, they confirm the high prevalence of dysfunctions in pOSA and highlight the need to develop a common language, strengthen care networks, and improve the integration of OMT in France.

papers.title: Using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health Framework to Document Real-World Functional Outcomes in Inpatient and Outpatient General Rehabilitation.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND The International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health (ICF) provides a standardized framework for documenting rehabilitation outcomes beyond diagnosis-based reporting. ICF qualifiers were recorded at baseline and at the end of rehabilitation for Body Functions, Activities and Participation, and Environmental Factors. RESULTS In Body Functions, significant reductions were observed in both profiles for energy and drive (b130), sleep (b134), emotional (b152), pain (b280), exercise tolerance (b455), urination (b620), joint mobility (b710), and muscle power (b730). In Activities and Participation, inpatient rehabilitation showed significant reductions across all analyzed codes, including daily routine (d230), body position (d410, d415), transferring (d420), walking (d450), self-care (d510-d550), looking after one's health (d570), interpersonal interactions (d710), and remunerative employment (d850). CONCLUSIONS ICF-based profiles captured multidimensional functional changes in routine general rehabilitation, while Environmental Factors complemented outcome assessment by describing supportive contextual resources.

papers.title: Orgasmic Meditation, Sleep, and Next-Day Somatic Distress: A 30-Day Observational Study.
papers.abstract: Orgasmic Meditation (OM) is a structured attention-training practice conducted between two people who follow a predefined set of detailed instructions. One person, the stroker, gently strokes the clitoris of the other person, the strokee, for 15 minutes while both place their attention on the point of contact and notice what they feel. Climax is not the goal. This study examined whether OM practice was associated with app-assessed sleep and next-morning Tumescence Survey responses. In this 30-day observational study, 41 experienced OM practitioners enrolled, and 36 contributed analyzable data, yielding 1,026 participant-nights. The Sleep Cycle Premium application assessed sleep quality, duration, regularity, and time to sleep onset. Each morning, participants reported whether they had practiced OM the previous day and completed the 15-item Tumescence Survey. Linear mixed-effects models accounted for repeated nights from the same participants and separated within-person from between-person associations. OM practice was not significantly associated with sleep quality (b = -1.87 index points; 95% CI: -3.96 to 0.21; p = .079), sleep duration (-10.11 minutes; 95% CI: -22.37 to 2.15; p = .106), time to sleep onset (+2.01 minutes; p = .225), or sleep regularity (+0.05; p = .948). On mornings after OM, participants reported less dissociation from their bodies and less agitation. These two item-level associations remained significant after correction for 15 comparisons. Craving and irritability scores were slightly lower after OM, but the differences were not statistically significant. Factor 2, which combined craving, physical discomfort, agitation, and dissociation, was lower after OM in the primary model (b = -0.77; 95% CI: -1.17 to -0.37; p < .001). The estimate weakened when the OM association was allowed to vary among participants (b = -0.67; 95% CI: -1.36 to 0.02; p = .056). Sleep did not mediate or modify this association. With OM practice and sleep duration in the same model, a day of OM was associated with the same reduction in Factor 2 as 3.8 additional hours of sleep (95% CI: 1.8 to 9.5), and with the same reduction in the total survey score as 1.7 additional hours (95% CI: 0.2 to 3.9). Climax was reported on 19.4% of OM days and was not associated with sleep outcomes within OM days. OM practice was not associated with app-assessed sleep in this sample. On mornings after OM, participants reported less dissociation from their bodies and less agitation, and these differences were not explained by sleep duration. The difference associated with an OM day was comparable in size to the difference associated with 3.8 additional hours of sleep for Factor 2 and 1.7 additional hours for the total survey score. The estimates weakened when the OM association was allowed to vary among participants. This comparison describes the relative size of observational associations and does not show that OM reduces sleep need. The sample was small and highly selected, and neither the sleep application nor the Tumescence Survey has been validated for this use. Controlled studies using validated measures are needed.

papers.title: Multimodal data integration for diagnosis and risk prediction of major depressive disorder in the UK Biobank.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) diagnosis currently relies on subjective assessments, limiting early detection and accurate risk stratification. To address this, we developed machine learning models for both prevalent diagnosis and 15-year incident risk prediction using multimodal data from 30,040 UK Biobank participants. We integrated six modalities-proteomics, metabolomics, lifestyle factors, family history, biochemical measures, and polygenic risk scores (PRS)-employing a geographically stratified design with England-based participants for training and those from Scotland and Wales for independent validation. The integrated multimodal model demonstrated superior robustness, yielding a stable mean time-dependent AUC of 0.679 for incident prediction and an AUC of 0.791 for prevalent diagnosis. Crucially, our analysis revealed that modifiable lifestyle factors, particularly sleep patterns, and proteomic profiles consistently outperformed polygenic risk scores, which showed limited independent discriminative ability. Notably, the diagnostic model exhibited high specificity, effectively distinguishing MDD from schizophrenia (AUC = 0.865), bipolar disorder (AUC = 0.799), and anxiety disorders (AUC = 0.729). Feature attribution revealed distinct molecular signatures for disease stages: inflammatory mediators including CTSL and MMP7 dominated diagnosis, whereas markers of neuroplasticity and metabolism such as LRRN1 and LEP emerged as key predictors of future risk. Furthermore, biological enrichment analyses implicated dysregulated immune regulation (specifically neutrophil degranulation), lipid metabolism, and signal transduction pathways, highlighting a potential mechanistic shift from metabolic vulnerability in the risk phase to systemic inflammation in the symptomatic state. These findings demonstrate that integrating multimodal data significantly improves the characterization of MDD, offering a scalable framework for objective biomarker discovery and personalized risk assessment.

For anxiety symptoms, both MBE subtypes were associated with significant improvements (all p < 0.05), with no significant difference observed between TC/qigong and Pilates/yoga. In terms of depressive symptoms, TC/qigong demonstrated significant improvement (p < 0.01), whereas Pilates/yoga did not yield a significant effect (p = 0.17). However, the difference between subgroups was not statistically significant (p = 0.14). Significant improvements were also observed for sleep quality (p = 0.01), fatigue (p = 0.001), and quality of life (p < 0.01) following MBE interventions. MBE significantly improves pain, fatigue, sleep, anxiety, depression, and quality of life in fibromyalgia patients. Subgroup analyses indicate that TC/qigong and Pilates/yoga show comparable efficacy in pain and anxiety reduction, while TC/qigong may offer additional benefits for depressive symptoms. papers.title: Association between the dietary index for gut microbiota and circadian syndrome: a cross-sectional study from NHANES 2007-2018.
papers.abstract: Circadian Syndrome (CircS) is an epidemiologic construct that combines metabolic abnormalities with features related to sleep and mood and has been associated with adverse health outcomes. The dietary index for gut microbiota (DI-GM) is a dietary proxy index reflecting adherence to dietary patterns potentially related to gut microbial composition, but its relationship with CircS remains unclear. A total of 18,491 adults from NHANES 2007-2018 were analyzed using survey-weighted logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) modeling, subgroup analysis, and sensitivity analysis. Associations between individual DI-GM components and CircS were further evaluated. Nine machine-learning algorithms were used to assess classification performance and model interpretability based on area under the curve, calibration, decision-curve analysis, and Shapley additive explanations. Mediation analyses were conducted to evaluate whether body mass index (BMI) and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) may partly account for the observed association. Higher DI-GM scores were inversely associated with CircS. Participants in the highest quartile had lower odds than those in the lowest (OR = 0.693, 95% CI 0.603-0.797; P for trend < 0.001). RCS analysis suggested an overall inverse association, with no strong evidence of nonlinearity (P overall < 0.001; P nonlinearity = 0.130). Subgroup analyses indicated possible variation by poverty-income ratio, ethnicity, and education. Several DI-GM components differed by CircS status. Machine-learning models showed moderate classification performance, and the incremental contribution of DI-GM was limited. Mediation analyses suggested that BMI, and to a lesser extent SII, may partly account for the association between DI-GM and CircS. Among U.S. adults in NHANES 2007-2018, higher DI-GM scores were inversely associated with CircS. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship between dietary patterns represented by DI-GM and CircS.

papers.title: Use of massage therapy for non-painful health conditions: an evidence map of systematic reviews.
papers.abstract: There is high- or moderate-certainty evidence that massage therapy is beneficial for certain painful conditions. Massage therapy has also been evaluated for a range of non-painful health conditions, but the extent and certainty of this evidence are less well characterized. We mapped the systematic reviews, conclusions, and certainty (quality or strength) of evidence for outcomes of massage therapy for non-painful health conditions. Computerized search of PubMed, AMED, CINAHL, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, and Web of Science from July 2018 to July 2024. This evidence map updates a Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) report that covered massage therapy reviews published through July 2018. Study selection included systematic reviews of massage therapy for non-painful adult health conditions that formally rated the certainty (quality or strength) of evidence supporting the conclusions. Systematic reviews of sports massage therapy, osteopathy, dry cupping/dry needling, and internal massage therapy (e.g., for pelvic floor pain), and self-administered massage therapy techniques (e.g., foam rolling) were ineligible. Main outcomes and measures include health condition, number of included studies, intervention, comparison group, conclusions, and certainty of evidence. A total of 13 systematic reviews of massage therapy for 8 non-painful adult health conditions were identified. Of 190 full-text reviews, 20 used a formal method to rate the certainty (quality or strength) of evidence supporting their conclusions; 7 reviews overlapped in health condition, resulting in 13 included reviews. Across these, one conclusion about abdominal massage therapy for functional constipation was rated as high certainty of evidence. There were 4 conclusions from 3 reviews rated as moderate certainty of evidence: 2 conclusions in 1 review about acupressure and auricular acupressure for improving sleep quality in patients with cancer, 1 conclusion about acupressure for sleep latency and fatigue in people with chronic kidney disease, and 1 conclusion about massage improving depressive symptoms in individuals living with dementia; all remaining conclusions were rated as low or very low certainty of evidence. Evidence on adverse events was collected by 7 of 13 (54%) reviews; serious adverse events attributed to massage therapy were not identified in those reviews, but adverse event data were often incomplete or inconsistently described. Only a small number of systematic reviews reported high- or moderate-certainty evidence supporting the potential benefit of massage therapy for specific non-painful adult health conditions. High-certainty evidence was limited to abdominal massage therapy for functional constipation, whereas moderate-certainty evidence indicated that acupressure and auricular acupressure may improve sleep quality in patients with cancer, acupressure may improve sleep latency and decrease fatigue in people with chronic kidney disease, and massage therapy may reduce depressive symptoms in individuals living with dementia. For most other non-painful adult health conditions evaluated, available conclusions are supported only by low- or very low-certainty evidence. Additional high-quality research is needed to strengthen the evidence base for massage therapy for non-painful adult health conditions, particularly for conditions and outcomes that currently lack at least moderate-certainty evidence.

papers.title: Identification of associative factors for recurrent respiratory tract infection using machine learning models in preschoolers.
papers.abstract: Childhood recurrent respiratory tract infection (RRTI) poses a significant global public health burden. This study aimed to identify factors associated with RRTI in preschool children using machine learning (ML) and to develop a web-based tool for estimating individualized RRTI probabilities. Two cross-sectional surveys using stratified cluster sampling were conducted in 2020 and 2025. RRTI was diagnosed according to the national criteria issued by the Chinese Medical Association and China Association of Chinese Medicine. Questionnaire data covering demographic characteristics, fetal/neonatal history, and lifestyle factors were collected. Total 15,075 eligible records from two surveys were included, reporting an RRTI prevalence of 14.55%. Ten ML models were trained on 29 candidate variables. The eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model outperformed the others, yielding an area under the curve of 0.733. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified sleep duration, child's age, and screen duration as the top three associative variables for childhood RRTI. Forward feature selection was applied to derive a parsimonious nine-variable predictive set, which was subsequently deployed as an online application ( https://cipchina.streamlit.app/ ). In a large, population-based cohort of preschool children, three factors (sleep duration, child's age, and screen duration) associated with RRTI were consistently identified across multiple high-performing ML models. This study identified key lifestyle-related factors associated with recurrent respiratory tract infection in preschool children. Ten machine learning models were applied to analyze 29 variables from 15,075 Chinese preschoolers, with further importance interpreted via the SHapley Additive exPlanations. Sleep duration emerged as the primary lifestyle-related factor associated with childhood recurrent respiratory tract infection, followed by child's age and screen duration.

papers.title: Criterion-related validity, classification accuracy, and misclassification patterns of the International Fitness Scale in adolescents from a rural Mediterranean region of Spain: The EHDLA study.
papers.abstract: Self-reported fitness instruments provide a scalable surveillance solution when objective testing is impractical, yet the nature of perception-accuracy discordance in adolescents is not well understood. This study examined criterion-related validity, classification accuracy, convergent construct validity against the Spanish Perceived Physical Literacy Instrument (S-PPLI), and misclassification patterning of the International Fitness Scale (IFIS) in a community sample of adolescents from the Valle de Ricote (Region of Murcia, Spain). Cross-sectional data from 1017 Spanish adolescents (471 boys, 546 girls; median age 14 years) from the Eating Healthy and Daily Life Activities (EHDLA) study were analyzed. IFIS overall correlated with the Assessing the Levels of Physical Activity and Fitness (ALPHA-Fit) composite (Spearman rho [ρ] = 0.369; partial ρ = 0.377, p < 0.001), with flexibility showing the strongest domain-specific validity (Spearman ρ = 0.635; partial ρ = 0.592, p < 0.001). Using the full five-level IFIS score, the area under the curve (AUC) for identifying the lowest fitness tertile was 0.66 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.63-0.69). At the primary screening cut-off (IFIS ≤ 3), sensitivity was 0.68, specificity was 0.59, and negative predictive value was 0.80, while a stricter threshold (IFIS ≤ 2) increased specificity (0.94) at the cost of sensitivity (0.16). Convergent validity with S-PPLI was supported (partial ρ = 0.56, p < 0.001). Misclassification profiling identified 18.5% of participants as underestimators and 17.6% as overestimators; underestimation was associated with shorter sleep, while concordant-low membership was associated with higher body mass index (BMI), lower activity, and more sedentary time. In conclusion, IFIS showed weak-to-modest criterion-related validity and limited discriminative accuracy. Therefore, IFIS may serve as a low-burden adjunct to objective testing for population-level prioritization, but its performance relative to other brief instruments or low-burden measures, including BMI, remains untested. Discordance between perceived and objective fitness was common (36.1%) and co-occurred with lifestyle and adiposity characteristics, supporting consideration of perception-accuracy profiling in school-based and public health surveillance. Findings pertain to a single rural region and require replication in urban, regional, and socioeconomically diverse samples before broader generalization.

papers.title: Comparing Fatigue Assessment Tools in Hemodialysis: Implications for Nephrology Practice From the Technology Assisted Stepped-Collaborative-Care Trial.
papers.abstract: Fatigue is a debilitating symptom experienced by patients treated with hemodialysis (HD). The standardized outcomes in nephrology-hemodialysis fatigue (SONG-HD-fatigue) and patient-reported outcome measurement information system (PROMIS-fatigue) instruments have not been used extensively among patients treated with HD. Our study evaluated the psychometric properties and treatment response of these measures compared to the commonly used functional assessment of chronic illness therapy-fatigue (FACIT-F) in HD. Technology assisted stepped-collaborative-care was a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of a stepped-collaborative-care intervention for symptom management in HD. Participants were adult patients receiving in-center 3-times-weekly maintenance HD at 14 dialysis units. We compared the performance of the SONG-HD-fatigue (3 items) and PROMIS-fatigue (7 items) against the FACIT-F (13 items) by evaluating their comparative psychometric performance (known-groups validity, convergent and divergent validity, screening utility, within-patient reliability, and responsiveness to treatment). Among participants (N =160; age 57.8 years, 35% female, 27% Black, and 15 % Hispanic), the median baseline FACIT-F score was 44. Patients experiencing higher baseline fatigue levels demonstrated significantly lower social support, physical function, physical activity, and sleep quality, and increased pain intensity, pain interference, depression, and anxiety. SONG-HD-fatigue and PROMIS-fatigue had similar direction and strength of correlations as FACIT-F with these outcomes. A SONG-HD-fatigue score of 4.5 and a PROMIS-fatigue score of 56.8 corresponded to a FACIT-F score of 30 for screening for clinically significant fatigue. The mean difference between the technology assisted stepped-collaborative-care intervention and control group at the 3-month primary outcome timepoint was significant for the PROMIS-fatigue and FACIT-F measures but not for the SONG-HD fatigue. Small sample size. SONG-HD-fatigue and PROMIS-fatigue had strong correlations with the validated FACIT-F questionnaire, suggesting that they can be helpful screening measures to identify patients treated with HD with significant fatigue. However, they were not as sensitive in capturing response to treatment.

papers.title: Translating Geroscience Into Clinical Practice: Molecular Targets, Emerging Therapies, and Lifestyle Strategies for Healthy Longevity.
papers.abstract: Population aging has intensified interest in interventions that preserve function and delay multiple chronic diseases by modifying the biology of aging. The field now spans molecular geroscience, experimental therapeutics, biomarker development, and preventive medicine, but the maturity of evidence varies substantially. This study aimed to synthesize foundational mechanisms, clinical and translational strategies, and lifestyle determinants relevant to healthy longevity, while distinguishing established practice from emerging or unproven interventions. A critical narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE and reference lists was conducted from January 2000 through August 2026. Priority was given to consensus frameworks, human randomized trials, prospective cohorts, systematic reviews, and influential mechanistic studies. Evidence was interpreted according to study design, clinical relevance, reproducibility, and safety. The expanded 12-hallmark framework depicts aging as an interconnected network involving genomic damage, impaired maintenance systems, maladaptive stress responses, inflammation, and dysbiosis. Senolytics, epigenetic reprogramming, nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) augmentation, mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibition, metformin, and spermidine are biologically plausible, but none yet has definitive evidence of extending lifespan in healthy humans. Epigenetic clocks are useful research biomarkers, although a lower clock estimate is not synonymous with rejuvenation or proven risk reduction. By contrast, cardiorespiratory fitness, muscle strength, dietary quality, restorative and regular sleep, avoidance of tobacco, management of cardiometabolic risk, and social connection are supported by much stronger human-outcome evidence. Responsible longevity medicine should integrate geroscience with rigorous preventive care, use biomarkers as adjuncts rather than diagnoses, and reserve experimental geroprotectors for well-designed trials. The near-term opportunity is not radical life extension, but compression of morbidity through scalable, equitable, and evidence-based preservation of health span.

papers.title: Quality of Life as a Pathway Linking Sleep Quality and Depressive Symptoms in Medical University Students: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Depressive symptoms are common among university students and are associated with poor sleep quality. However, it remains unclear whether the association between sleep quality and depressive symptoms is direct or operates through quality of life (QOL). Screen time may also be associated with sleep quality. This study examined whether QOL mediates the association between sleep quality and depressive symptoms among medical university students, with screen time specified as an upstream behavioral factor of sleep quality. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 150 students aged 19-24 years. Sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and QOL were assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale, and WHOQOL-BREF (Taiwan version), respectively. Partial least squares structural equation modeling with 5,000 bootstrap resamples was used to estimate the structural paths and indirect associations. Longer screen time was associated with poorer sleep quality (β = 0.338, p = 0.001). Poorer sleep quality was associated with lower QOL (β = -0.374, p < 0.001), whilst higher QOL was associated with fewer depressive symptoms (β = -0.614, p < 0.001). Although the total association between sleep quality and depressive symptoms was significant (β = 0.327, 95% bootstrap CI [0.120, 0.477], p < 0.001), the direct association was not (β = 0.097, p = 0.212). The specific indirect association through QOL was significant (β = 0.229, 95% bootstrap CI [0.119, 0.327], p < 0.001), consistent with an indirect-only mediation pattern. Sleep quality was indirectly associated with depressive symptoms through QOL within the specified structural model, while longer screen time was associated with poorer sleep quality. These findings highlight QOL as a central consideration in understanding the association between sleep quality and depressive symptoms, alongside screen-use behaviour in relation to sleep health. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships among these variables.

papers.title: Acupuncture-Assisted Zolpidem Tartrate Tapering and Discontinuation in Patients with Chronic Insomnia Disorder Stabilized on Zolpidem: A Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: The prevalence of chronic insomnia disorder (CID) is relatively high and increases with age. The use of sedatives, along with the incidence of their adverse effects, is also rising, which can easily lead to health risks and negative outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of acupuncture-assisted zolpidem tartrate tapering and discontinuation in patients with CID whose insomnia symptoms are clinically stable while taking zolpidem. This study is designed as a single-center, single-blind, randomized controlled trial.Ninety participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the acupuncture group or the sham acupuncture group. Each participant will undergo 24 sessions of either acupuncture or sham acupuncture, in conjunction with zolpidem tartrate tapering therapy, over a duration of 8 weeks, followed by a 4-week follow-up observation period. The primary outcome is the discontinuation rate of zolpidem tartrate at week 8. Secondary outcomes include the reduction rate of zolpidem tartrate, the discontinuation rates at weeks 10 and 12, frequency of zolpidem tartrate use (nights/week), average daily dose (mg/day), total weekly dose (mg/week), Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Generalized Anxiety Disorder -7 (GAD-7), Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), Short Form Health Survey-12 (SF-12), sleep diary-related indicators, Dysfunctional Beliefs and Attitudes about Sleep Scale -16 (DBAS-16), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) and emergency medication usage. Adverse events will also be monitored throughout the study. Efficacy analyses will be conducted on the intention-to-treat population. The findings of the study may provide preliminary evidence for standardized protocols for reducing and ceasing zolpidem tartrate use through acupuncture assistance. Additionally, this research may offer useful references for patients with CID seeking to safely and effectively reduce or discontinue zolpidem tartrate. These findings may inform future clinical research and larger multicenter confirmatory studies.
